To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrasound cleaning and nitrogen jet cleaning are unsatisfactory for removing particulate matter from moss samples.

ultrasound cleaning treatment should be discarded because of the transfer of extracellular metals to the water in cleaning, and that nitrogen jet cleaning is unacceptable because it damages the phyllids or alters the membrane permeability, and does not eliminate the particles.
the best way to remove particles that are not bioaccumulated in the tissue of the moss P. purum is to clean the moss by hand with a soft brush.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an accurate and reliable method to remove particles from the moss tissue and to distinguish the proportion of metal bioconcentration and the proportion that remains on the moss surface.
the determination of a suitable technique to eliminate the particles attached to the plant surface without altering the moss tissue.
the development of an accurate method to distinguish between metal bioconcentration and particulate matter attached to the mosses, and the best method for cleaning the moss surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
none of the methods tested were able to eliminate the particles from moss surface and therefore, the bioconcentration of metals in moss tissues could not be accurately determined.
the best method to remove the particles attached to the surface of the mosses without altering the membrane permeability is to wash the moss with distilled water.
the mosses are a good indicator of the bioavailability of metal pollutants in the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sequential elution method is the most suitable method for eliminating the contaminants that are not incorporated into the moss cells.
the use of moss as biomonitor should be restricted to those metals that are bioconcentrated and not to those that are only adsorbed at surface.
the sequential elution is the best technique to remove the extracellular metal from the moss surface and that the nitrogen jet and ultrasound techniques should be discarded.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sequential elution method should not be used to differentiate between the bioconcentrated fraction and the non-bioconcentrated fraction, but it should be applied as a cleaning method for moss samples.

the use of moss as a biomonitor is limited by the lack of knowledge of the proportion of metals that are not bioaccumulated, which are not removed by the washing procedures used in the traditional methods.
the use of moss for biomonitoring purposes should be restricted to the determination of bioconcentrating processes and that the determination of adsorption processes should not be performed.
